facts.statement: Threshold is nearly inert over most of its range on the built-in image.
facts.evidence: The image is almost binary: background 0 plus noise, blobs 185-255. Counts at min size 20 and 'bright': threshold 0.05 to 0.74 all give 16 objects; 0.76 gives 16; 0.78: 18; 0.80: 13; 0.84: 10; 0.90: 7; 0.95: 5; 1.0: 6. At min size 1: 16 for 0.05-0.74 then 18,41,89,72,67,42,60,20,35,46,31,35,181 for 0.76..1.0, and 0.01 gives 7785. Above ~0.76 blobs fragment into noise specks (visible in rendered sheet.png). So the threshold slider is dull over 0-0.75 and ragged above; min size carries the story: at threshold 0.5 counts are 16 (1-50 px), 13 (100), 7 (200), 4 (300), 2 (500). 'dark' mode returns 3 (background plus the two ring holes) for threshold >= 0.3 and min <= 100.

facts.statement: Sliders can drive REAL results without fabrication if every grid cell is a real function output, because the pipeline is a plain threshold.
facts.evidence: Min size has only 65 distinct outcomes across its 500 values, so the client only does a lookup (threshold stop, min size) to result id. A refusal is also a real output: the real tool raises ToolError 'No blob found (threshold 0.95, at least 500 pixels): lower the threshold or the minimum size.' (tour.py:58); the grid contains this as a real message. Caveat: threshold must be quantised to the precomputed stops (0.05 step, or finer: 0.01 steps cost 101x500 runs, about 25 min offline, not completed). The slider snaps; it should say 'precomputed example results'.

findings:
SUMMARY
The Feature tour is real, released (in 0.0.1), deterministic, small and runnable, and a real-results slider demo from a precomputed grid is technically easy and honest. But it is a poor FIRST example: it is a bridge test fixture on a synthetic image, listed on the site under 'Testing and maintenance', without any real screenshots, and its threshold slider is inert over 75 % of its range.

WHERE IT LIVES
- Tool: LabConstrictor-Playground/src/labconstrictor_playground_lc_tools/__init__.py:136-176. Function: src/labconstrictor_playground/tour.py (demo_image:12-28, segment:31-64). Test: tests/test_tour.py:12-17 (16 objects, 256x256 uint8, reproducible) and lc_tests/cases.json:162-186.
- Inputs: image (None = built-in demo), region, look_for bright/dark (radio, default bright), threshold 0..1 (slider, default 0.5), min size 1..500 px (slider, default 20), side_note (folded, auto-cleared). Outputs: blobs label image, outlines (GeoJSON polygons), centres (y,x,label,area_px), measurements table (label,y,x,area_px,mean_intensity), summary text 'Found **16** blob(s). (the built-in demo image)'.
- Default result: 16 objects. Areas: 81 (x3), 149, 197 (x6), 253 (x3), 317 (x2), 500 (x2 rings). Centres of rings fall inside the hole (a red dot in the middle of the ring, which looks odd but is the real centre of mass).

RUN
Scratch venv with scipy, pandas, pytest and the Tools package (network allowed, no system install). Playground tour tests: 4 passed. The decorated feature_tour(...) is directly callable, so I generated every result via the REAL declared tool (including labels_to_shapes outlines), not a port. Scripts and output in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/a3a6ac4f-1857-5992-b7c5-06332778d500/scratchpad/demo-feasibility/playground/ (grid.py, dedupe.py, full.py, build_asset.py, render.py, tour_cell.py, sheet.png, asset_005/grid.json + demo.png).

GRID RESULTS (bright, counts)
5 thresholds x 4 min sizes (rows 0.3, 0.5, 0.75, 0.85, 0.95; columns min size 10, 20, 50, 100): 16,16,16,13 / 16,16,16,13 / 16,16,16,13 / 10,10,10,9 / 5,5,5,5. First three rows are identical: a naive evenly spaced grid exposes the plateau. Min size at threshold 0.5: 1->16, 50->16, 100->13, 200->7, 300->4, 500->2. Threshold sweep at min 20: 0.05-0.76 -> 16, 0.78 -> 18, 0.80 -> 13, 0.82 -> 11, 0.84 -> 10, 0.86 -> 11, 0.88 -> 8, 0.90 -> 7, 0.95 -> 5, 1.0 -> 6. Refusal: (0.95, 500) and threshold 1.0 with min >= 50 give the real ToolError text. Dark: 3 objects for thresholds 0.3-0.9 (background plus two ring holes), meaningless as a showcase.
Rendered sheet.png: default and large-min-size results look tidy (yellow outlines, red centres on white discs/rings on black); thresholds >= 0.8 shows fragmented speckle outlines, which is honest but ugly. The image is flat-colour discs, not convincing fluorescence microscopy (no cytoplasm texture, no varying size/shape beyond discs).

ASSET SIZE (the user's question)
- Meaningful sweep: thresholds 0.05..0.95 step 0.05 (19) x min size all integers 1..500 = 9,500 real runs, only 65 distinct results; store each distinct result once and a run-length index. Measured for 21 thresholds including 0 and 1: 85 distinct successful results, 413 KB raw / 21.6 KB gzip, index 5 KB raw / 1.25 KB gzip; background PNG 27 KB. A simple 228-combo grid without dedup: 1.16 MB raw / 22.7 KB gzip; with dedup 207 KB raw / 11.5 KB gzip. 5x4 grid: 3.8 KB gzip. All far below any budget; sizes are not a problem. Generation: 10,500 runs 332 s on this box (including outlines).
- The client only looks up a result id; nothing is computed or invented. Honest label: 'Precomputed from the real Feature tour code on a fixed synthetic image; sliders snap to precomputed values.'

NOTEBOOK CELL (change in Playground repo, to propose separately)
No tour cell exists in main or in 0.0.1. Minimal addition, tested headlessly in the scratch folder (tour_cell.py, run with stubbed widgets: default gives 16 rows, threshold 1.0 / min 500 prints the real 'No blob found' sentence): after the Make test data cell add a markdown cell '# Step 3: Feature tour' and a code cell that imports `from labconstrictor_playground.tour import demo_image, segment` and `from labconstrictor_tools import ToolError`, builds widgets.RadioButtons (bright, dark), FloatSlider threshold 0..1 default 0.5, IntSlider min size 1..500 default 20, a 'Run the feature tour' button and an Output; on click it calls segment(...) (catching ToolError and printing it), draws imshow + ax.contour(labels>0, [0.5]) outlines + red centres, shows 'Found N blob(s) (the built-in demo image)' and display(pd.DataFrame(rows)). About 30 lines, uses only numpy/scipy/pandas/matplotlib already in requirements.yaml; same style as the existing cells; also bump notebook version and changelog, and update the intro text. Alternatively call feature_tour directly from labconstrictor_playground_lc_tools. Needs a new Playground release to appear in the installed app.

MANIFEST / HONESTY / SHOWCASE VALUE
- The Playground is section: testing and is presented as 'not for analysing your data'. A demo whose headline is a test fixture would reinforce the 'this is a test, not science' impression and confuse the 'Use an app' story; scientists will see 'blobs on black' not microscopy.
- Positives: its manifest honestly declares hosts [notebook, napari, fiji, qupath]; the bridge is exactly what the Feature tour was built to show (slider, radio, folded group, five output types), so it is the right fixture for an 'architecture / one declaration, many hosts' explainer, with the same tool and results across Notebook, Napari and Fiji views.
- Negatives: no real screenshots of this tool in any host (the only real host captures are NucleiSky/CellTracksColab/synthetic Kitchen sink), so host views would be redrawn UIs; the notebook cell does not exist yet; the data are simple discs; the threshold slider is inert for 0-0.75.

COMPARISON WITH NUCLEISKY AS FIRST EXAMPLE
- Visual appeal: NucleiSky (real fluorescence-like image with real QC figure, banner, bridge screenshots N2/N5/F2/F3) is far more convincing; Feature tour is plain discs with speckle artefacts at high thresholds.
- Honesty: Feature tour wins on host claims (manifest declares hosts and has a real bridge test); NucleiSky manifest advertises only notebook, so host views must carry the 'experimental' label. For Feature tour, results are real outputs of the real code; for NucleiSky registration, only recorded values can be shown.
- Interactivity without fabrication: Feature tour yes (grid lookup, 85 real results, about 21 KB gzip); NucleiSky registration only static recorded outputs plus opacity/toggle controls.
- Real artefacts: NucleiSky yes; Feature tour no (screenshots would have to be taken: needs the Napari/Fiji plugin installed and run, not done here).
- Audience value: NucleiSky is something a biologist wants to use; Feature tour demonstrates the framework, not a scientific use.

RECOMMENDATION FOR THE PLAN
Use NucleiSky as the primary scientific example and consider a small 'try the bridge' module based on the Feature tour as a secondary, clearly labelled illustration (or a later replacement of the placeholder interactivity in the architecture section) rather than the front door. If the Feature tour is used, ship the deduplicated grid (<= 25 KB gzip), use thresholds weighted to 0.70-0.95 or a non-linear mapping, expose min size 1..500 with the real refusal message, drop the 'dark' option or keep it with an explanation, and cut the 'blobs in two parts' wording.
risks: Threshold plateau: 0.05-0.76 gives identical results, 0.78-1.0 fragments blobs; a 'threshold' slider will look broken or boring unless its stops are chosen carefully and explained.

Provenance: results were produced with numpy 2.5.3 / scipy 1.18.1 / pandas 3.0.6, not the pinned 2.0.2 / 1.16.3 / 2.2.2 of the app; scipy.ndimage.label and numpy default_rng are stable, but a published grid must record versions and the Playground commit, and ideally be regenerated with the pinned stack.

Site rules: no numpy/scipy in site requirements; generated files must be git-ignored while a precomputed grid has to be committed or fetched; the build must never go online and must have one source of truth. A committed grid is a vendored copy of another repo's behaviour that goes stale if tour.py changes (needs a checked generator script, version stamp and a test comparing the 16-object default to the Playground test).
DESIGN.md and check_design.py have no pattern for sliders/radios/Run buttons in content (buttons only for copy and clear filters); a design-rule update is required.

Showing the tool as a Napari/Fiji window would be a redraw: no real captures of the Feature tour exist and it is unverified that it has been exercised in Napari/Fiji by humans (not in the clean-test report). Napari/Fiji/QuPath hosts are labelled 'Soon' on the app page, so claiming them risks overclaiming.

Framing: the app is in the 'Testing and maintenance' section and says 'not for analysing your data'; putting it on the home page tile as a microscopy workflow may mislead, and the synthetic discs may look like a toy to scientists.
The README/Description 'blobs in two parts' is not true of the demo image; do not repeat it.

The notebook route is unavailable: the released app has no Feature tour notebook cell; a notebook view of the Feature tour would be a mockup of something that does not exist until a Playground change is merged and released.
Pure client-side lookup may be read as 'running the analysis in your browser'; the disclaimer must say results are precomputed and the sliders snap to them.
recommendations: Do not make the Feature tour the first example; keep NucleiSky (or another real microscopy example) as the front door. Use the Feature tour at most as a secondary 'one tool, many hosts' illustration, where its honesty about hosts and its five output types fit.

If built: ship a deduplicated grid generated by the real feature_tour: thresholds 0.05 step (or denser, e.g. 0.01 steps, about 25 min offline) x min size 1..500, 85 distinct results, ~21 KB gzip plus ~27 KB background PNG; include version/commit stamp and the real refusal text; snap sliders to stops; keep a test that the default cell equals 16 objects.
Choose slider stops or labels so the interesting region is visible (threshold 0.7-0.95 and min size 1-500); say plainly that 0-0.75 does not change anything on this image because it is nearly binary.

Generate the grid with the pinned Playground stack (numpy 2.0.2, scipy 1.16.3, pandas 2.2.2, Python 3.12) and store it as a documented vendored asset (README with provenance), not as a hand-edited file; the generator can live outside the site build because the site must not import scipy.

Propose separately in the Playground repo: a 'Step 3: Feature tour' notebook cell (about 30 lines, in the scratch tour_cell.py), a notebook version bump, changelog and a release, so that a real notebook view of the same analysis exists.

Capture real Napari and Fiji screenshots of the Feature tour (needs the plugins installed) before any host view of it; otherwise show host views as the generic form diagrams or reuse the real NucleiSky captures and label them accordingly.
Fix the README and Description wording 'blobs in two parts' in the Playground (or make the image really contain them).
Before adding sliders or a Run control to the site, extend DESIGN.md and check_design.py narrowly (in-page control class) as an explicit rule update.
open_questions: Does the user want the demo to show the framework (bridge, same tool in notebook/Napari/Fiji) or a science workflow? The Feature tour fits the former, NucleiSky the latter.
Is the Playground owner willing to add a Feature tour notebook cell and cut a release (0.0.2) so the notebook view is real?
Has anyone run the Feature tour in Napari/Fiji/QuPath and can supply real screenshots, or must they be taken? Not in the clean-test report.

Should the committed grid live in the site repo (vendored, with provenance) or be fetched from the Playground repo at fetch time (needs a new published artefact there)? The site's no-generated-files and single-source rules need a decision.
Which threshold stops and step (0.05 vs 0.01) does the user prefer, and should 'dark' be shown at all?

Should the demo's synthetic image be replaced by something more convincing (for example the Tools celltracks or nucleisky fixtures) at the cost of losing the Playground's tested 16-object ground truth?
